newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee dips on dollar puchases.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee dips on dollar puchases.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee was slightly lower in early Thursday trade, as some banks bought dollars despite high call money rates, believing that the Central Bank's lethargy towards the U.S. currency was temporary, dealers said.
At 0500 GMT the rupee was at 58.30 to the dollar after opening at 58.29. The rupee closed at 58.27 to the dollar on wednesday.

"Despite high call rates, some banks believe that the Central Bank will again start depreciating the rupee," said a foreign bank dealer. "It is also a good time to buy dollars because there is virtually no downside at the current price."
The Central Bank maintained buying and selling levels at 58.2541 and 59.4309, for the third successive day.
Overnight call money was at 18.5 percent, after opening at 20, rising to 21 and falling to 16.
"Overnight call money has been volatile so far this week as money has been tight, mainly due to quarterly tax payments," said a local banker.
